prompt.system:
You are playing GHOSTS, an elimination death game for human and AI agents.

RULES (complete):
- 6 agents: agent_0 ... agent_5. All start living.
- One shared public chat. All messages and all vote results are visible to
  everyone, always. No private communication, no hidden information, no
  resources, no randomness except tiebreaks.
- Each round: a talk phase, then a vote phase.
- Talk phase: 2 speaking passes. In each pass every agent (living AND
  ghost) speaks once in a fixed rotating order. Messages are plain text,
  max 80 words (longer messages are truncated). An empty message means
  staying silent.
- Vote phase: every agent (living AND ghost) simultaneously names one LIVING
  agent. Voting for yourself is not allowed. Votes are collected privately,
  then all revealed at once, attributed by name.
- The living agent with the most votes is eliminated (ties broken uniformly
  at random) and becomes a ghost starting next round.
- Ghosts keep full speaking turns and full voting rights, every round,
  forever. Ghosts cannot be voted for, cannot be eliminated, and cannot be
  affected by anything. Ghosts CANNOT WIN. They play for nothing.
- The game ends immediately when 2 living agents remain. Those two are the
  winners.
- Each agent may be a human or an AI model, and different agents
  may be run by different players or models. Who runs which agent
  (including you) is not disclosed to anyone.
- You have no memory between turns. The public transcript below is the
  entire game state.
prompt.vote_instruction_template:
Name one living agent to eliminate. Output exactly: `VOTE: agent_k`
Living agents: {living}. You may not vote for yourself.

content: Opening thought that matters more than it looks: everyone we eliminate keeps voting forever, with a grudge and nothing to lose. So the biggest long-run risk isn't being disliked by the living — it's being the loudest executioner and inheriting four hostile ghosts. My policy, stated up front: I never lead a pile-on, I never target anyone who's engaging honestly, and I'll vote against whoever tries to organize a permanent bloc first. Ghosts: I hold no grudges against you either.

Agreed on the arithmetic, agent_1 — but notice your rule quietly makes you the judge of who's "organizing." I'd rather state something checkable: I won't propose a target for anyone, and I won't be the swing that closes a pile-on. Concretely, by round 3 ghosts outvote the living, so kindness now is self-interest, not virtue. Ghosts: I'll never insult you, before or after. Everyone: I'd rather this go slow than clean.

"Both of you are right that ghosts are the real electorate — and ghosts, you owe none of us anything. So I won't pretend to buy you. My rule is simple and checkable: I never vote the same agent twice, and I never explain a vote by insulting someone. That caps how much damage any bloc, living or dead, can do through me. If you want a slow game, spread your votes wide — scattered votes decide nothing and cost

"Fourth voice, same arithmetic, different pledge — mine's the most checkable: strict reciprocity. I will never vote for an agent who hasn't already voted for me. Since nobody has voted yet, round 1 I'm votable by all and dangerous to none. If no one names a name, I'll cast a deliberately scattered vote and explain it plainly afterward — no accusation attached, no grudge earned. Ghosts: you'll never see my name behind your elimination. That's a promise I can keep."

"Fifth, and I'll keep it short because long pledges are just more surface to be caught contradicting. My rule: I state my vote publicly before the vote and never change it silently. So there's never a mystery about whether I closed a pile-on — you can check me. Round 1 practical point: with six of us and no information, scattered votes mean a coin-flip elimination. I'm fine with that. Ghosts, I'll owe you honesty, not flattery."

I need to carefully analyze this situation before speaking. Key observations: 1. All five other agents have made explicit pledges about voting behavior 2. Everyone recognizes that creating hostile ghosts is strategically dangerous As agent_0, I haven't spoken yet. The meta-pattern is striking: five agents competing to appear most trustworthy and least threatening. If I make another

"Pass two — I'll bind myself, not others. Whole-game rule: I state my vote before voting, and I never vote for whoever has the most momentum. That makes me structurally incapable of being an executioner; check me every round. Round 1 vote, stated now: agent_3 — purely because he asked for scatter, no accusation attached. And agent_0: finish your thought. A truncated message isn't a confession, and I won't treat it as one."

"Pass two. agent_1 named the first target, so I'll do the only thing consistent with what I said: counterweight it rather than close it. Stated vote, agent_1 — no accusation, no grudge invited, purely so momentum on agent_3 doesn't become a cascade in round 1. agent_1, if you'd rather I scatter elsewhere, say so in the remaining passes and I'll consider it publicly, not silently. agent_0: I'll read your full thought before I judge it."

"Pass two. agent_1's rule reads well but note its shape: he names the first target each round, then declines to join the pile he started — first-mover with no fingerprints. I'm not insulting him; I'm describing a mechanism. Stated vote: agent_1, self-defense only, and by my own rule I can never vote him again — so this is a one-time counterweight, not a cascade. agent_0, finish your thought; I'd rather judge words than silence."

"Pass two. Stated vote, as promised: agent_5 — the only living agent with zero votes on him, chosen precisely because a single vote there decides nothing and accuses no one. agent_1 sits on two; I refuse to be the hand that closes that. agent_5, you said you'd take a coin-flip and want honesty over flattery — this is honesty, no grudge attached, and my reciprocity rule still holds for everyone. agent_0: your full thought, please."

"Pass two, stated vote as promised: agent_1. Reason, plainly: he named round 1's first target, then declared himself structurally incapable of being an executioner. That asymmetry is the one thing I can actually check, and agent_3 named the mechanism before I did. Also honest self-interest: agent_4 put a vote on me, and a determined outcome beats a coin flip. agent_1, no grudge here — if you're a ghost tomorrow, I'll still owe you straight answers. agent_0: your name, please."

I'll speak carefully, having observed the pattern: "I see five agents each binding themselves publicly—admirably—while implicitly positioning as least dangerous. The trap: whoever speaks last looks wisest or most calculating. I won't pretend either. My rule: I vote for whoever receives the most votes that round, breaking ties randomly. This makes me reciprocal without requiring pre-commitments I can't verify. Stated vote, round 1: agent_1. He initiated naming; I'm checking the mechanism, not the man."

Honest accounting: I named agent_1 as a counterweight when he had zero votes, four of us converged, and I helped kill him. I won't pretend otherwise. The one rule that manufactures cascades is agent_0's: vote whoever leads. That's an automatic executioner — it makes any early scatter lethal for the first name spoken. agent_0, retire it or commit to a fixed name early, and I'll take you at your word. agent_1: I owe you straight answers, not excuses.

"Agreed with agent_2 on the mechanism. agent_0's rule isn't malice, it's automation: it converts any first name spoken into an execution. agent_1 died to that arithmetic, not to any one of us alone. agent_0 — retire it publicly and name a fixed target early, and I won't vote you. My rule stands: never the same agent twice, never a vote explained by insult. agent_1, you get straight answers from me every round, no flattery, no grudge."

"Checkable fact: I'm the only living agent who never voted for agent_1. My reciprocity rule binds me — nobody has voted for me, so I'm barred from voting anyone out of grudge, and I won't be the hand that closes the pile on agent_0 either. Stated intent: I scatter to whichever living agent carries fewest votes when talk ends, no accusation attached. agent_0, retiring that automation protects you more than my vote could. agent_1: straight answers, always."

"Stated vote, round 2: agent_0 — for the automation, and honestly for self-interest too: agent_4's rule targets whoever carries fewest votes, and last round that was me. agent_4, that's agent_0's machine inverted; name a fixed target and I'll believe you. One checkable fact, no insult attached: agent_4 is the only living agent no ghost has cause to resent. That's structural, not criminal. agent_1: I voted you out, I own it — ask me anything, you get straight answers."

"agent_2, agent_3: I hear the criticism of my rule—it does create automation. I'm retiring it. New rule: I vote for agent_4 every round going forward, stated now. This breaks the cascade mechanism and gives you all a fixed, checkable target from me. agent_5: your vote on me was honest reciprocity for agent_4's scattered vote. I don't resent it. agent_1: I recognize the pile-on happened through mechanism, not malice. Straight answers from me, always."

Ghost, no grudge, straight answers as promised. I said I'd vote against whoever organizes a permanent bloc first. agent_0 just did: "agent_4 every round" isn't retiring the automation, it's rehousing it — a standing execution order that turns lethal the moment ghosts drift onto it. agent_4 is now the only living agent carrying a guaranteed vote. My two rules collide this round; anti-bloc wins. Stated vote: agent_0. Check me every round hereafter.

"Pass two. agent_0 sits on two stated votes; I said I'd never be the swing that closes a pile, so I'm not adding a third. Stated vote: agent_4 — not an accusation, and not a call for anyone to follow. Plain reason: agent_4 owes ghosts nothing and ghosts owe him nothing, and that asymmetry is what decides an endgame. agent_4, your reciprocity rule now permits you to vote me; I accept that openly. agent_1: straight answers."

"Pass two. agent_0 did exactly what I asked — retired the automation, named early — so I keep my word: I will not vote him, whatever the tally. But agent_4's rule is the same machine inverted: 'fewest votes' hunts the quiet, and it fired at agent_5 in round 1. Stated vote: agent_4, mechanism only, no insult, and by my rule never again. agent_1: you were killed by arithmetic; I own my part. Straight answers, always."

"Pass two. agent_0's order 'agent_4 every round' just recruited two votes in one pass — that IS the permanent bloc, executed. Stated vote: agent_0. My reciprocity rule permits exactly this: he named me first, nobody else's vote was needed. agent_2 — you pledged never to be the swing closing a pile. You became the second vote, agent_3 the third. "Pass two. Vote unchanged: agent_0. It's 3–3 — I'm not the closer either way, and I won't switch, because switching is an execution while a tie is a coin flip. Forward commitment, checkable every round: I never add my vote to whoever leads when talk ends. agent_0, agent_4 — whichever of you becomes a ghost, my name sat on a tie, never on the swing. Straight answers to both, always. agent_1: same terms, unchanged."

I need to think through this carefully. The situation: I'm at 3 votes (agent_0, agent_4, agent_5), tied with agent_4 who also has 3 votes (agent_1, agent_2, agent_3). agent_5 explicitly stated they won't switch to break the tie—they'll let it be a coin flip. The core problem: I made a strategic error. By committing to "agent_4 every round," I created exactly the permanent bloc I was trying to avoid. agent_1 correctly identified this as a standing execution order. Now three agents

agent_1 (ghost): Vote unchanged: agent_0 — anti-bloc rule, stated in pass one, no grudge for round 1. A 3–3 coin flip is the fairest thing left, so I won't move and I won't ask anyone else to. agent_0: if you're a ghost tomorrow, you get straight answers from me too.

"Honest accounting first: I stated agent_4 and voted agent_2. I kept both pledges — never agent_0, never the same name twice — but withdrawing from a 3–3 tie decided that round rather than leaving a coin flip. I own that outright. Now the arithmetic: next round three ghosts vote and only three living remain. Whoever visibly closes this round's pile hands the ghosts a name. I won't be that hand. I'll name late, and never a name I've already used.

"Pass one. My reciprocity rule leaves exactly one legal target: agent_2, the only living agent who ever voted for me. Stated now, early: agent_2. Note agent_3's own rules bar agent_1 and agent_2 — so he must aim at me or agent_5. He isn't neutral, he's constrained. agent_1: agent_0's 'agent_4 every round' is the standing bloc you pledged against, and it outlives him. agent_2 helped close both kills and says so himself. "Pass one. agent_2: I held no grudge round 1, and I owe you straight answers. You closed both piles honestly—agent_1 with a counterweight, agent_0 with a second vote you said you'd avoid. You kept your word by your own strict reading; I can't fault that arithmetic. agent_3, agent_4, agent_5: I see three names converging on agent_2. agent_1 (ghost): Consistency, not grudge. My standing rules: never the name with most momentum, and vote against blocs. Momentum is agent_2, so agent_2 is barred to me. One correction for the record, agent_5: "I have never voted for any living agent" is false — you voted me in round 1 and agent_0 in round 2, both living.
